title: Input symbol in an encoded state
statement: Let $R$ be a number of registers, let $\Lambda$ be a label set, let $P$ be a counter program, let $x$ be an input bit string, and let $s$ be an abstract program state with read position $p$. If $p\le |x|$, then the symbol under the input head in the machine configuration encoding $s$ is the possibly absent bit $x[p]$ (with zero-based indexing).
hypotheses_covered: Counter program register count $R$ and label set $\Lambda$
replaced:
Let $x$ be an input bit string of length $n$ and $s$ an abstract state of a counter program over
$R$ registers whose read position $p$ satisfies $p \le n$. Then the symbol under the input head
in the machine configuration encoding $s$ on input $x$ is the bit $x_p$ (indexing from $0$) when
$p < n$, and no symbol (a blank) when $p = n$.
